Japan under Allied military occupation, led by the United States, from 1945 to 1952. The map shows it in 1945.

Japan surrendered in August 1945, after the atomic bombings and the Soviet entry into the war. General Douglas MacArthur took charge as Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers. The occupiers ruled through the Japanese government, and the emperor kept his throne but gave up any claim to be divine.

The changes went deep. Women voted for the first time in 1946. A new Constitution of Japan took effect in 1947; it made the emperor a symbol of the state and, in Article 9, renounced war. Land reform broke up large estates and created a nation of small farmers. The big family business groups were split, unions were allowed, and wartime leaders were tried at the Tokyo trials.

As the Cold War and the Korean War began, the aim shifted to rebuilding Japan as an ally. The Treaty of San Francisco ended the occupation in April 1952, though Okinawa stayed under American rule until 1972. The story goes on in Modern Japan.
sum: Japan under Allied military occupation, led by the United States, from 1945 to 1952. The map shows it in 1945.
